clinician.final_diagnosis: bilateral femoral neck insufficiency fracture caused by heroin-induced osteoporosis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 55-year-old male with 30+ years of intravenous heroin use presented with 6 months of bilateral hip pain, claudication, and lower limb weakness. Initial workup revealed severe osteoporosis (DEXA T-scores -3.2 spine, -4.0 bilateral hips) and multiple insufficiency fractures on MRI (bilateral femoral neck, bilateral sacral ala, thoracic/lumbar spine) with corresponding hot spots on bone scan. Laboratory evaluation showed elevated alkaline phosphatase, hypophosphatemia, hypocalcemia, low 25-(OH)D3, and hyperphosphaturia with inappropriately normal PTH (48.1 pg/ml) despite metabolic abnormalities, consistent with renal phosphate wasting secondary to heroin-associated tubular dysfunction. Renal function was normal (creatinine 0.85 mg/dL). The patient underwent bilateral hip hemiarthroplasty for the femoral neck fractures. Six months post-treatment, laboratory parameters normalized (25-(OH)D3 38.3 ng/ml, phosphate 2.9 mg/dL, calcium 8.8 mg/dL), confirming recovery from the metabolic bone disease.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Severe osteoporosis documented by DEXA with T-score -3.2 (spine) and -4.0 (bilateral hips)
Bilateral femoral neck insufficiency fractures, bilateral sacral ala insufficiency fractures, and multiple thoracic/lumbar spine lesions on MRI
Multiple hot spots on whole-body bone scan indicating metabolic bone disease activity
Metabolic abnormalities consistent with renal phosphate wasting: hypophosphatemia, elevated urine phosphate, hypocalcemia, low 25-(OH)D3, with inappropriately normal PTH (48.1 pg/ml)
Normal renal function (creatinine 0.85 mg/dL) excluding renal failure as cause of bone disease
Long-standing intravenous heroin addiction for more than 30 years as etiologic factor
Bilateral hip hemiarthroplasty performed for femoral neck insufficiency fractures
Recovery of metabolic parameters at 6 months: 25-(OH)D3 normalized to 38.3 ng/ml, phosphate to 2.9 mg/dL, calcium to 8.8 mg/dL

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Not explicitly ruled out by SPEP/light chains in available records, but clinical pattern of reversible metabolic abnormalities and specific association with heroin use makes this less likely
PTH was normal (48.1 pg/ml, reference 15-68.3) rather than elevated
Creatinine was normal (0.85 mg/dL) with normal renal function

remaining_uncertainties: No documented serum protein electrophoresis or free light chain assay to definitively exclude multiple myeloma
No documented urinalysis for glucose or amino acids to definitively confirm Fanconi syndrome, though the pattern of phosphaturia with hypophosphatemia and normal renal function is highly suggestive
Specific medical therapy details (doses of vitamin D, calcium, phosphate supplementation) not explicitly documented, though metabolic recovery implies appropriate treatment
